rationale: Consolidate the parent account so it carries all four witnessed consequence classes, including the two compaction ones that until now lived only in the child accounts. The rewrite names the cause once, cites each class with its receipt and decisive events (per-replica index inflation and lost reconfiguration endpoint; the one-index-per-round drift; the leader's decision at a drifted index; and the two compaction paths, where trim compacted 7 for six indices of content and snapshot(Some(8), false) produced a snapshot holding none of the five decided entries), keeps the same-run controls and the counterevidence that bounds each class, and lists the child knowledge entries it relies on so the linkage is recorded rather than implied.

interpretations.rationale: One index-space error in the StopSign accounting, four witnessed classes of consequence, each in its own receipt. Cause: sync_log adds the StopSign carried by a LogSync on top of sync_idx plus the suffix length while the sender's resume point may already count that StopSign, and create_log_sync never shifts sync_idx for a StopSign the sender already holds. (1) A replica that already accepted the configuration's StopSign and receives a coverting resume point ends one index past its content: follower after reconnected() (9125b6a531234e7d9d2fa8cbb817df63 event 35), follower re-promising in an ordinary new term with no reconnected() call (6cdcff36336646859bffb9e8c3e39789 event 11), the leader that takes over from such a follower (dda5bb4179154e3abe90e69f5267b3ea event 13), and two followers under a snapshot-capable entry type (fd0b8be59c8f466fbf7768abb08f93b5 events 51, 52). Each such replica stops reporting its reconfiguration as decided and its decided-log read loses the entries (one element or nothing against six before). (2) The index drifts one step per re-synchronization round rather than settling: three consecutive reconnection rounds took the followers from 7 to 8 to 9 over unchanged content and the leader's decided index followed (6c879304cdde4ddd8e1640207cdbf94d events 41-49). (3) A write quorum of drifted reports makes the leader decide the reported index although it holds fewer entries (8b314551f1e049fcbf73a358f8ddf2c8 and 9125b6a531234e7d9d2fa8cbb817df63 event 24; snapshot-capable: fd0b8be59c8f466fbf7768abb08f93b5 event 53), after which the leader no longer reports the reconfiguration as decided and its decided log is unreadable. This decision needs two drifted reporters in a three-node cluster: with one, the leader stayed consistent (9125b6a531234e7d9d2fa8cbb817df63 event 37; 6cdcff36336646859bffb9e8c3e39789 event 9). (4) Both compaction paths inherit the drifted values and act on them: trim(None) took the minimum recorded accepted index, which had drifted above the leader's content, and compacted index 7 for a log of six indices, with the region then reported trimmed (ec3329dc273e452aa92bcd44652c116a events 9-15); snapshot(Some(8), false) was accepted inside the drifted decided index, advanced the compacted index to 8 and produced a snapshot holding none of the five decided entries the log contained, so the entries are no longer reachable and the snapshot that represents them is empty (e70b8baa087246c78ea3a64f24b8e97c events 0-5). Both calls returned success on input the documentation allows. Controls: the pre-change samples and the no-reconnect control kept six indices of content, a six-element decided log, the StopSign at its own index and the reconfiguration reported as decided (8b314551f1e049fcbf73a358f8ddf2c8 events 9-11, 19-21; 6c879304cdde4ddd8e1640207cdbf94d events 38-40; fd0b8be59c8f466fbf7768abb08f93b5 events 48-50).

knowledge.assertion: sync_log adds the carried StopSign on top of sync_idx plus the suffix, and each further re-synchronization adds another index
the decided-log read loses the entries after such a re-synchronization
the condition is the resume point covering the StopSign's index
the leader decides the reported accepted index without bounding it to its own log
a candidate leader syncing from a follower is inflated in its own accepted index
the recorded accepted and decided indexes drift one index per re-synchronization round
trim accepted a drifted bound and compacted past the content the leader held
the snapshot path accepted a drifted bound and produced a snapshot holding none of the entries

counterevidence: The no-reconnect control kept every endpoint consistent (accepted 6, decided 6, is_reconfigured true, six-element decided read: 8b314551f1e049fcbf73a358f8ddf2c8 events 9-11), and in the newterm case the new leader and the node that received nothing stayed consistent (6cdcff36336646859bffb9e8c3e39789 events 9, 10), so the deviation follows a re-synchronization whose resume point covers the StopSign.

The leader-side decision at a drifted index requires a write quorum of drifted reporters in one term (two of three nodes); one drifted reporter left the leader consistent (9125b6a531234e7d9d2fa8cbb817df63 event 37; 6cdcff36336646859bffb9e8c3e39789 event 9).

The compaction consequences need the drift to cover every node the bound is derived from: trim's bound is the minimum recorded value, so a truthful replica would keep it honest (76cabb0efc3b4eda8eda8c9c79025550-interpretation-0), and the snapshot witness used a request strictly inside the drifted decided index because the StopSign equal case lowers the bound.

The documented reconfiguration flow expects a new instance once a node observes StopSign(ss, true), narrowing the window in which a user reads the old instance; the drift still hides that observation from the leader and, once compaction acts, removes the entries themselves.
limitations: The drift was exercised for three rounds by construction; no bound on rounds or counter values, and no automatic repair inside the sealed configuration, was established.
Loss-triggered and timer-triggered re-synchronization were not exercised; the producers observed are explicit reconnected() calls and ordinary leader changes with one node cut off.

Only three-node clusters were used, with in-memory storage, no persistence across restarts and one snapshot-capable entry type; the compaction witnesses depend on that entry type's snapshot semantics.

Several comparisons in the repeated-rounds, trim and snapshot receipts came out unknown because their admissions shared event names across cases in one execution; those states are asserted from the sampled operands, with the violated comparisons cited above.
The consequence set stays within index accounting, readability and compaction; the sealed configuration admits no further entries, so no value is mis-assigned.
interpretations.joint_history: Eight receipts of one harness lineage, each read on its own samples and never combined arithmetically: 8b314551f1e049fcbf73a358f8ddf2c8 (resync, control), 9125b6a531234e7d9d2fa8cbb817df63 (single resync, read of index 6), 6cdcff36336646859bffb9e8c3e39789 (newterm), dda5bb4179154e3abe90e69f5267b3ea (staleleader), fd0b8be59c8f466fbf7768abb08f93b5 (snapshot-capable resync), 6c879304cdde4ddd8e1640207cdbf94d (three reconnection rounds), ec3329dc273e452aa92bcd44652c116a (drift then trim) and e70b8baa087246c78ea3a64f24b8e97c (drift then snapshot). Each successor reproduces the earlier witnesses and adds one case.
